title: Finished working on my first AI game
author: Hocekklocek
selftext:
This is a post to close the first chapter in my AI game dev journey.

I have spent many hours going back and forth with Claude Opus 4.6 trying to make my 'Kernel Panic' clicker game. After feedback from people who took the time to play my game a couple months ago I spent time and made improvements to the tutorial and flow of the game. The hardest part is definitely balancing the whole thing. I still dont feel like the game is fully balanced, however Claude is not able to balance it properly for me and I dont think I can do it any better without changing every value manually... so this is it for now.

If you would like to see the final result of my Kernel Panic project feel free to try it on itch [Kernel Panic](https://hocek.itch.io/kernel-panic)

Now onto the next one! I will be able to make something a lot better with the experience I have gained making this simple clicker game.

comments.author: lundrog
comments.body: Book marked to try later. You cool with chatting about your process? Im also exploring ai game development

replies.author: Hocekklocek
replies.body: Yesh we can chat but theres not much to it, I just use claude code to write the game code and test myself

replies.author: lundrog
replies.body: No steering on what to use? Or best practices or guardrails to follow?

replies.author: Hocekklocek
replies.body:
Make sure you write precise prompts on what you want, if you have a lot that you want done in one promot make it detailed and ask the AI to create a plan and then it can work through the plan in small chunks rather than trying to do everything in one go. Definitely save game states/versions(version control) so you can always go back if something goes very wrong.

I am still quite new to this and I have heard of all these AI workflows and skills for claude you can use for game development that I have yet to try

replies.author: lundrog
replies.body: I made my own guardrails which helps. What models you been using?

replies.author: Hocekklocek
replies.body: Opus 4.6 mainly, tried the others but they use too many token and are overkill for what I needed so far
